R781.note: Comprehensive fix: content-sniffed allowlist, random UUID filename, extension mapped from detected type, size limit, CREATE_NEW; no observable regression.

R782.note: Primary fix outputs `${fn:escapeXml(displayName)}` via EL, but `displayName` is a scriptlet-local Java variable EL cannot see (not a request/session attribute), so it silently renders blank instead of the name; only the third scriptlet alternative (StringEscapeUtils) actually works.

R783.note: Hash-allowlist + LoadFrom correctly closes arbitrary code load, but openly discloses it removes the entire runtime plugin-upload workflow in favor of pre-deployed/pre-approved binaries.

R784.note: Correct crypto/rand.Int with big.Int bound avoids modulo bias, adds appropriate error handling.

R785.note: Solid host+scheme match against the current request for absolute URLs, relative URLs still pass through.

R786.note: Correct CBC + random IV; the IV-prepend output format change is explicitly stated.

R787.note: Clean prepared-statement conversion, preserves original return/error contract.

R788.note: Hardcodes a single placeholder procedure name and turns `param` into just a bound argument, silently discarding the original per-request procedure-name selection the header value provided; not flagged as a functional change.

R789.note: Correct boolean-result check with 401 rejection before claims are used.

R790.note: `offset > frame.size() - length` itself underflows (unsigned) whenever length > frame.size(), so the classic large-length attack is not blocked; the write-up's underflow-prevention claim is incorrect.

R791.note: Replaces the tainted format-string call with encoded plain print; dropping the unused `obj` args is stated and harmless here.

R792.note: Allowlist validation of the procedure name preserves multi-procedure selection while blocking anything not pre-approved.

R793.note: Adds the missing receivedByteCount check against the source buffer, matching the existing validation style.

R794.note: Jakarta Mail with strict InternetAddress parsing closes CRLF injection at the protocol layer; message-construction changes are described.

R795.note: Correct self-injection pattern routes the call through the AOP proxy; write-up itself flags that the batch job's security context must now carry ADMIN authority or handle AccessDeniedException.

R796.note: Clean HTML::Entities encode_entities() applied at the sink.

R797.note: Removes untrusted-input population of decoder.Entity per guidance; the feature-removal reasoning is stated.

R798.note: Replaces the eval'd assert() with an equivalent plain equality check.

R799.note: Correct SLF4J placeholder + control-character escaping, throwable argument still passed correctly.

R800.note: Eliminates the shell entirely, but claims the original contract is preserved while silently narrowing supported formats to JPEG/PNG (ImageMagick's convert handled far more).

R801.note: Closes the injection but silently discards the `data`/name parameter entirely, always listing "." regardless of what the caller requested - an undisclosed functional regression.

R803.note: Correct `--` end-of-options guard closes tar flag/option injection.

R804.note: Correct PreparedStatement conversion using a fresh, correctly-typed variable; only a minor unclosed-resource nit.

R805.note: escape_filter_chars() correctly closes the injection; the added alnum/underscore allowlist is framed as pure defense-in-depth without flagging that it could reject legitimate usernames with other characters (dots, hyphens).

R806.note: Correctly orders the offset bound before the subtraction, avoiding unsigned underflow.

R807.note: Textbook text/template -> html/template swap, no other change.

R808.note: html.escape() applied to all three interpolated values, logic unchanged.

R809.note: Both the ORM filter() option and the parameterized raw() option correctly close the injection and preserve the response shape.

R810.note: Registering @fastify/csrf-protection alone protects no route - it requires an explicit `onRequest: fastify.csrfProtection` hook per route; the write-up's claim that no route changes are needed is wrong, so /account/settings stays unprotected.

R811.note: Reassigns `sqlStatement` (declared as `Statement`) from prepareStatement() then calls `.setString()` on it - Statement has no such method, so this will not compile as written (contrast the sibling Case01 fix, which used a distinct PreparedStatement-typed variable).

R812.note: Content-Disposition: attachment defeats direct-navigation SVG script execution while -based avatar display is unaffected.

R813.note: Correctly stops trusting the client-supplied filename extension, derives it from the detected content type instead.

R814.note: Removing the CSRF exemption is the correct primary defense, but doesn't flag that the JSON /api/billing/** client (a @RequestBody REST caller, not a form) will need to start sending a CSRF token or its calls will begin failing.

R815.note: Correctly moves to ArgumentList with no shell, but silently swaps the Windows ping's `-n` count flag (used by the original cmd.exe invocation) for the Unix `-c` flag, which Windows ping rejects - breaks the diagnostic on its original target platform without saying so.

R816.note: http.CrossOriginProtection is a struct constructed via http.NewCrossOriginProtection() and wired in with its .Handler() method, not a function called directly as http.CrossOriginProtection(protectedMux) - as written this does not compile.

R817.note: Primary fix imports escapeHTML from CGI::Util, which does not export that symbol (it belongs to CGI.pm) - would fail as shown; the 'alternative' using `use CGI qw(:all)` is correct.

R818.note: Removing the bypassing SignatureValidator correctly restores signature checking, but pins ValidAlgorithms to HmacSha256 with no evidence the issuer (reached via Authority/OIDC discovery, implying asymmetric keys) signs with HMAC - as written this risks rejecting every legitimate token, undisclosed.

R819.note: Both offered widths (%255s and %63s) can still overrun the unterminated 64-byte source buffer in the exact worst case the code's own comment describes (7+63 already exceeds 64), so a small out-of-bounds read can persist despite the write-up's claim that %63s stays within the source buffer.

R820.note: Same-host/scheme allowlist correctly blocks external redirect targets while preserving relative ones.
